posts.content:
Last year at Ather Community Day, we unveiled Redux which is a concept vehicle that embodied everything we aspire to be as a brand: technology-led, futuristic, and obsessively crafted down to the smallest detail.

Redux wasn’t really created to answer a market need or fit into a product segment. It was created to ask a simple question: If we reimagined personal mobility from first principles, what would it look like?

What makes Redux special, however, isn’t just the vehicle itself. It’s the people behind it.

A small team that came together with a bold idea to rethink a two-wheeler from the ground up. Starting with the most fundamental elements of mobility, they stripped away assumptions and built everything around the essentials: the rider, the battery, and the wheels. What began as a rough sketch soon became a shared vision that inspired an entire team to rally behind it.

The challenge was bringing that vision to life without compromising its essence. Every component, every mounting point, every structural element had to be reconsidered and refined repeatedly to preserve the purity of the original form while making it a fully functional machine.

Concept vehicles often remain static explorations of design. Redux was different. The team was determined to make it real, to create something that could move, respond, and be experienced.

Beyond the form, the team also designed the soul of the vehicle. How should it react when a rider approaches? How should it communicate, respond, and build a sense of connection? The goal was to build a companion, something that feels alive and instinctive in the way it interacts with its rider.

The making film we released this week is a glimpse into that journey. A story of curiosity, craftsmanship, persistence, and a team that refused to settle for “good enough.”

Because behind every concept that pushes boundaries, there’s a group of people willing to challenge them first.

Watch the entire video via the link in the comments below.

posts.content:
Future of all interfaces on a two wheeler - voice!

We have been excited about it for a long time. Ather Energy pretty much invented the concept of touch screens on 2Ws (being the first to do that on a production bike), and we continue to invest heavily into capabilities and feature sets on it.

But even as we push the envelope on that front (almost half of our vehicles today ship with a touch TFT and 100% ship with on-board compute and connectivity) we believe the future could very well be one that does not need you to glance at the display at all.

Using LLMs and natural language processing and bundling that inside our smart helmets (Halo) we believe that being able to ‘just tell’ your scooter what you want can be super intuitive.

In fact, far more intuitive than stationary applications like mobile phones, laptops etc. On a scooter you can’t operate touch while riding, and we would rather have you glance as little as possible when in heavy traffic or at high speeds. Being able to just tell your Ather what you want, especially inside the cocoon of your helmet (or on any Bluetooth headset really), is a significant tech and experience upgrade for riders:

Navigation:
“Take me to Nandi Hills,”
“Navigate home,”
“Let’s go to Cubbon Park,”
“How far is the nearest charger?”
“ETA to jaljog choraha?”
"Time to stadium circle?"

Vehicle Settings:
“Decrease brightness,” or “Maximum brightness,”
“Change Traction control to Rain,”
“Magic twist, High,”
“Share my live location.”

Calls:
“Call Rohit” - This is fully integrated with your existing contact list.

Media controls:
“Play the next song”
“Pause”

We unveiled it last year and have finally rolled out Voice on Ather to all our Gen 3 and above customers now. Do give it a try!

Voice today is just the starting point. We believe we can build a ton of experiences for our riders on top of this capability.
Next upgrade (soon): your Ather will talk and recommend things to you. Alerts, suggestions, feedback - proactively.

posts.content:
8 years ago, the Ather 450 launched.

The night before, on 3 June 2018, we were sitting in a basement with paintbrushes and tiny cans of touch-up paint. Fixing final details. Sticking on decals. Wiping everything down one last time. That’s the kind of people who end up at Ather, people who don’t just witness the story, they #BeTheStory.

The next morning, most journalists walked in expecting the Ather 340, the scooter everyone knew was coming. When Tarun said “say hello to the 450,” the room exploded. They rode it and noticed the throttle, the touchscreen, the way it handled details we had argued over for months, finally out in the world.

Eight years later, the 450 is a landmark. India’s first electric scooter with a touchscreen dashboard, navigation, and performance that changed what people expected from their rides entirely.

What it also proved is something we’ve believed since day one: that people who care deeply about their work build things that last.

Here’s to the team that stayed in that basement. And to everyone who has joined since, carrying the same instinct forward.

#AtherEnergy #Ather450 #ElectricVehicles

In 0.1 seconds, an Ather scooter can detect and recover from a slide. The average human reaction time is 0.25 seconds.

That gap is where the magic happens. B G Gautham’s latest piece on the Ather Tech Review maps out the four specific layers where a vehicle can intervene: keeping itself in working condition, catching rider behavior before it turns dangerous, compensating for what the road does, and responding after a crash when the rider no longer can. What makes the argument land is not any single feature, but the cumulative case that the hardware to do all of this already exists inside a modern EV.

The real work now is standardisation, getting these capabilities defined, validated on Indian roads, and mandated as a baseline rather than left as a premium option. Worth reading if you think about where the ecosystem is headed.

Full analysis is in the article. Link in the comments.

#AtherStack #AtherEnergy #EVSafety #Engineering #ThinkAsASpecies #BeTheStory

posts.content:
Some things you build as a company.
Some things you build with an ecosystem .

LEAF has been a big part of the second. Something that we truly believe in is that the future is electric and because of that building the ecosystem around that belief becomes just as important as building the vehicle itself.

After months of conversations, back and forth, and a lot of people coming together behind the scenes, we’re glad to share that the The Light Electric-Vehicle Acceleration Forum (LEAF) was launched yesterday, in the presence of Honorable Minister Shri H D KUMARASWAMY

For us at Ather, as a founding member alongside Vida powered by Hero MotoCorp and IPEC India, this has been a different kind of build.
It has been something that only works if multiple organisations choose to align.

And that’s really what LEAF is about.

As EV adoption scales, especially across two and three wheelers, charging becomes a key part of the experience. And today, that experience still needs to become simpler, more reliable, and more consistent.

LEAF brings together OEMs, charging providers, component players, and technology partners to work on this collectively, advancing interoperability, improving reliability, and building a more seamless charging experience for users.

But what stood out most through this journey wasn’t just the outcome.
It was the people.

The number of conversations it took. The willingness to rethink. The effort to build something that contributes to the ecosystem.

With 20+ organisations coming together at day zero, there’s a clear signal of where the ecosystem is headed.

LEAF is built on a simple belief: the next phase of EV growth in India will be driven as much by collaboration as it is by innovation.

#LEAF #LEEC #EV #AtherEnergy

Think about the people who’ve shaped your growth at work.

Chances are, they didn’t just give you advice. They shared their experience, trusted you with responsibility, or encouraged you to take a step you weren’t sure you were ready for.

At Ather, many of us can trace our own journeys back to moments like these.

That idea sits at the heart of this year’s International Women’s Day theme - Give to Gain. The belief that when we invest in each other’s growth by sharing knowledge, trust, and support, progress multiplies for everyone.

To open Women’s Month at Ather, we came together for a conversation around what this theme really means in the context of our workplace.

The discussion reflected on how organisations move forward when different perspectives work together. Real progress doesn’t happen when one group moves ahead alone. It happens when people actively create space for others to contribute, challenge ideas, and lead.

It also touched on what inclusion looks like in everyday work life. Not through big announcements or policies, but through moments like someone trusting you with an opportunity, someone sharing their experience so the next person can move faster, or someone encouraging you to step forward even when you’re unsure.

And when that happens, something interesting unfolds.

Confidence grows. People take bigger bets on themselves. And over time, the same support gets passed forward to someone else.

That’s the spirit behind Give to Gain, and a fitting way to begin a month where we celebrate the many women across Ather who contribute to this culture every single day.

#InternationalWomensDay2026 #IWD #GiveToGain #AtherEnergy #BeTheStory

Can a crèche be more than just a facility at work?
Can it reflect the culture of the people around it?

Ather began in a college classroom. Two students building something they believed in. Over time, that idea grew into a company, and the people who built it grew too. Many of those early hires, and many who joined along the way, are now in completely different stages of life.

At IBC Knowledge Park, where our HQ is based, a new crèche has recently opened on campus.

As our teams evolve, so do their needs. For working parents, access to dependable child care shapes how they plan their day, how present they can be, how confidently they show up.

Over the past several months, we stayed closely engaged with the IBC team through the process, knowing how meaningful this would be for our people.

When working parents drop their children off and step into their workday, what they carry with them is peace of mind.

And that makes a lot of difference.

Grateful to the IBC team for bringing this space to life.

Culture isn’t always reflected in the biggest launches. Sometimes, it’s visible in the everyday decisions that support your people as they grow. 

#BeTheStory #AtherEnergy #PeopleOfAther

posts.content:
Good engineering is about eliminating guesswork. So is good medicine.

At this month’s TBC (The Boring Conference), we hosted Dr Vinod Scaria, Chief Data Officer at Karkinos Healthcare, and one of the key figures in India’s work on genomic medicine. He walked us through how personal genome sequencing is shaping the future of healthcare.

The idea is simple, but powerful. Every person’s DNA carries insights about how their body reacts to medication, which health risks they are likely to face, and what treatments are safe or unsafe for them. The challenge is turning that information into something usable in everyday clinical care.

This is not a futuristic pitch. It is already in use. Across India, networks like GUaRDIAN (Genomics for Understanding Rare Diseases India Alliance Network), which Dr Scaria co-founded, are helping doctors catch rare diseases earlier. These tools are being used to build health maps, identify which medicines work best for which people, and reduce trial and error in treatment.

Why talk about this at Ather?

Because the more we build technology that interfaces with human lives, the more we need to understand systems that are complex, personal, and data-dependent. Whether it is mobility or medicine, both rely on data to improve outcomes and reduce risk. 

We are grateful to Dr Vinod Scaria and the Karkinos Healthcare team for making the science accessible, and for sharing how this work is saving lives across the country.

There has been growing buzz around rare-earth materials over the past few months. Supply uncertainties, shifting export policies, and global dependency have pushed magnets into the centre of EV conversations in India and elsewhere. The topic is technical, but the implications are real for anyone building or thinking about the future of electric mobility.

Our team has put together a three-part series that looks at this space from different angles. Each instalment is written by a different member of the team so we can bring clarity to a subject that usually stays buried in jargon.

Part 1 is written by Athira Rajiv. She goes back to the basics of magnetism, explains why rare-earth elements matter, and breaks down the differences between different magnet grades. This foundation sets up the next two parts, which look at motor-level requirements and the global value chain.

If you want to understand the fundamentals behind rare-earth discussions and how they connect to India’s E-mobility ambitions, this is a good place to start.

What is the future of performance vehicles? For us, it starts with Redux.

Redux is our concept vehicle. It is what we envision for the future. With Redux, we want people to experience what Ather truly stands for. Our teams went back to the drawing board, with a vision to design a rideable concept vehicle. We explored the evolution of our design language from something clean and minimalistic to something bold and radical. 

The journey from a sketch to building a rideable prototype was an interesting one. We took an inside-out approach, went back to first principles, and developed a grounds up Aluminum chassis with a vertically placed battery pack. With that as a base, we created a new species - one that combines the agility and nimbleness of a scooter and performance and thrill of a motorcycle.

With Redux, we wanted to create experiences that ensure a bond between the rider and the machine. A vehicle that is ‘alive’, one that knows the intent of the rider more than the instruction and reacts to it. 

A performance vehicle designed for the users of tomorrow. 

#AtherEnergy #Redux #ConceptVehicle #EV
